newsitem.title: DUBAI: Indians, Saudis, Nepalis believed on Saudi jet.
newsitem.headline: Indians, Saudis, Nepalis believed on Saudi jet.

text.p: People believed travelling to Saudi Arabia on the Saudi jumbo which crashed on Tuesday included 215 Indians, 13 Saudis, nine Nepalis, three Pakistanis, three Americans and a Briton, a Saudi newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The English-language Saudi Gazette printed a passenger list, which it said it received from Saudi officials in New Delhi, of people scheduled to board the Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp Boeing 747 to Saudi Arabia.
Shortly after taking off from New Delhi airport, the plane collided in mid-air with an incoming Kazakh Airlines Ilyushin Il-76 freighter at a height of about 15,000 feet (4,570 metres).
All 351 people aboard the two aircraft died, Indian officials believed. The toll makes the collision among the world's five worst air disasters and the worst mid-air disaster.
Indian officials said there were 312 people, including 23 crew, on the Saudi flight SV 763, bound for Dhahran and Jeddah.
Airline officials in Jeddah told Reuters they have not yet issued a list of passengers that had boarded the plane.

The newspaper list showed the 23 crew comprised 12 Saudis -- five of them security men -- three Tunisians, three Moroccans, two Indians, one Jordanian, one Filipino, and the co-pilot -- an American citizen of Indian origin.
The list of passengers scheduled to travel included 213 Indians, nine Nepalis, three Pakistanis, two Americans, a Briton, a Bangladeshi and a Saudi.
The paper said 186 passengers, including two infants, had been bound for the eastern town of Dhahran while 103, including one infant, were due to go to the Red Sea port of Jeddah.
It said the parents of the Indian consul general in Saudi Arabia, Afzal Amanullah, were among the victims. They had been travelling to the kingdom to visit him.
The Saudi airline on Wednesday set up an emergency telephone line in Jeddah for enquiries by the families of the victims, a statement, quoted by the official Saudi Press Agency, said.
